scope: Native shared branding, launcher and package integration; Docker/Nginx/Compose and website CI configuration. Website application source is reviewed separately.

resolved_findings.issue: AUR and standalone RPM recipes referenced published v2.0.0 archives but unconditionally required brand files that those archives do not contain.
resolved_findings.resolution: All four AUR recipes now conditionally install the paired symbol and desktop entry. RPM uses a paired conditional install and a generated optional brand file list for %files -f. Current published archives remain packageable; future release archives still enforce brand asset presence.

resolved_findings.issue: Unrelated email redaction placeholders replaced public AUR maintainer metadata.
resolved_findings.resolution: The original maintainer metadata is restored in all four AUR files.

reviewed_behavior: SVG geometry and PNG/ICO/ICNS generation share the same source; transparent and monochrome variants are coherent.
Linux icon installation is idempotent and refuses foreign icon collisions; removal preserves modified icons.
Windows standalone installer carries an embedded ICO, shortcuts use a stable installed icon, and Windows Terminal profile changes preserve unrelated profiles and existing backup behavior.
Windows resource embedding checks CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS at build-script runtime and is a build-only dependency.
Docker build includes Rust catalog and brand inputs, pins base image digests, and configures nonroot UID101 on port8080 with a health endpoint.
Compose contains only the namespaced termfetch-studio-web service, read-only root filesystem and temporary storage; it introduces no shared proxy, database or network override.
Nginx configuration has SPA fallback, explicit missing-asset 404s, compatible CSP, HTML revalidation, hashed asset caching and graceful shutdown.
Website CI and deployment documentation match the monorepo build and namespaced deployment model.
limitations: This is source and recorded-evidence review, not a fresh native Windows/macOS display test.
Windows target linking and Explorer/Terminal rendering still require native Windows CI or QA; macOS .command remains a Terminal document rather than an app bundle.
Full final website container build and live deployment smoke checks remain the leader's next validation step after website integration.
